item.title: China takes two diving golds as Lin, Wang claim 1m titles
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
TOKYO, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China maintained its dominance in diving at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games by winning both 1m springboard gold medals here on Monday. Lin Shan and Long Yiping finished 1-2 in the women's 1m springboard. Li scored 263.05 points for gold, while Long finished second with 254.25. South Korea's Kim Su-ji took bronze with 245.05. Although Lin remained consistent throughout the five rounds, she said she was not fully satisfied with her performance. "Although the result is quite good, I am not very satisfied with the process," Lin said. "I didn't show my strengths. Each dive was stable, but not elegant or refined enough." Lin said her strengths usually lie in her lines and entries, but neither had been perfectly executed on Monday. "I have to set high standards for myself. If I don't demand enough of myself, I can't reach the world's top level," she said. Lin, who won silver at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023, said reaching the top of the podium after several years of hard work gave her further motivation. "After all these years, I've come this far, and my results have improved. I need to be more determined and keep moving forward," she said. For Long, who was making her Asian Games debut, a mistake on her fourth dive cost her valuable points. Her 107C earned only 33.00 points, leaving her eighth in that round. "It was more regret than disappointment, because I lost too many points on that dive," Long said. "But this is something I can adjust in training. That dive has already passed, so I was more focused on doing the upcoming one well." Long bounced back with a strong final dive, scoring 57.20 points for her 5333D. "I was very excited to take part in the Asian Games. The venue and environment here are excellent. As for my performance, I still have some shortcomings that give me more areas to improve in training," she said. Long said she hopes to compete at more international events and work toward the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. In the men's 1m springboard, Wang Zongyuan added another gold for China with 442.75 points, well ahead of South Korea's Kim Yeong-nam, who scored 373.30. China's Liu Chengzan took bronze with 361.45. Wang led from the opening dive and topped the standings in four of the six rounds. His highest score came on his fourth dive, a 405B, which earned 81.60 points. Despite successfully defending his title, Wang said there was still room for improvement. "I'm very happy to stand on the top of the podium and successfully defend my title from the Hangzhou Asian Games," Wang said. "But there were still many shortcomings throughout the competition, and I'll work on them in training." Wang said he had not fully settled into his competition rhythm in the opening rounds. "Maybe it was the first two dives. I didn't immediately enter the competition mode or reach the right level of excitement. I was distracted a little," he said. "Fortunately, I gradually found my competition rhythm in the later rounds." Liu, making his Asian Games debut, made a costly mistake on his third dive, a 205C, scoring just 36.00 points and dropping to fourth after the round. He recovered with 73.60 points on his fourth dive and eventually secured bronze. "I'm definitely not satisfied. To be honest, today's performance was quite far from the level I showed in training," Liu said. After the mistake, Liu said he tried not to dwell on it. "Once I made the mistake, I told myself not to think about that dive anymore and to focus on the dives ahead. There were still opportunities, so I just wanted to slowly make up the points," he said. Looking ahead to Tuesday's 3m springboard competition, Wang said he would focus on himself. "My goal hasn't changed. I hope to do my best tomorrow," he said. "The biggest challenge is still myself." ■

item.title: A glimpse of Yuanyang Hani Terraces in SW China's Yunnan
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Villagers harvest rice in Aichun Village of Yuanyang County in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, southwest China's Yunnan Province, Sept. 21, 2026. Listed as a World Cultural Heritage Site, a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System, and a World Heritage Irrigation Structure, the Yuanyang Hani Terraces vividly demonstrate China's ecological wisdom of "harmonious coexistence between humans and nature." Today, the millennia-old mountain farming in the terraced fields is taking on a new look. The terraces are nestled in the Ailao Mountains along the southern bank of the Red River in Yunnan. For centuries, fragmented plots, steep slopes and narrow paths had forced farmers to carry rice sacks on their backs or with horses. Today, drones can transport grain directly from paddy edges to village rooftops, reducing transport costs and shortening the transport time from 40 minutes to less than 10 minutes. New planting technologies are also easing farmers' workloads. A degradable paper-film embedded seeding and fixed-point planting technology developed by the School of Agriculture of Yunnan University has been applied in Niujiaozhai Town of Yuanyang County, allowing farmers to complete a full day's transplanting work in two to three hours. Local agricultural authorities have also improved rice varieties and introduced rice-fish-duck farming to raise household incomes. While new technologies support farming, the ancient terraces still rely on the participation of local people, who maintain and repair ditches to keep water supplies stable and prevent terraces from being abandoned. To protect the terraces, it is critical to let farmers share the fruits of economic development. Cooperatives here have boosted sales of local red rice via e-commerce and distributed profit dividends to farmers. Azheke Village, nestled in the heart of the terraces, has embraced a unique approach to tourism development. Villagers have contributed resources such as terraces, houses and traditional ways of life, creating a model of collective participation and shared prosperity. The improved livelihoods have drawn young rural migrants back home. In Duoyishu Village alone, over 80 homestays are now in operation, with more than 100 returning youths working in tourism, catering and transport sectors. In Yuanyang, the annual rice harvest now means far more than a good crop. It embodies a dynamic balance between ancient heritage protection and modern development, ensuring that the millennia-old terraces stay cultivated, local communities stay prosperous, and the unique farming legacy endures for generations. item.title: China's deep-sea drilling capacity reaches 5,000-meter level
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
An aerial drone photo taken on July 28, 2026 shows China's ocean drilling vessel Mengxiang conducting an operation at night. China's Mengxiang ocean drilling vessel has set a national record for deep-sea drilling, elevating its capability to the 5,000-meter level, after obtaining basalt samples from the South China Sea basin, the Ministry of Natural Resources said on Monday. This marks China's entry into international advanced ranks in deep-sea drilling operation capacity, according to the ministry. (Photo by Zhang Fatao/Xinhua) GUANGZHOU, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China's Mengxiang, meaning Dream, ocean drilling vessel has set a national record for deep-sea drilling, elevating its capability to the 5,000-meter level, after obtaining basalt samples from the South China Sea basin, the Ministry of Natural Resources said on Monday. This marks China's entry into international advanced ranks in deep-sea drilling operation capacity, according to the ministry. A 4.27-meter basalt sample was extracted during the voyage via a self-developed drill, which made China the third country after the United States and Japan to obtain hard rock samples from a deep ocean basin using drilling vessels. The research team conducted a long-term and high-intensity operation of shipborne remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), deploying two ROVs to operate for over 358 hours in total at a depth of 4,000 meters, with a single continuous operation lasting up to 103 hours, reaching internationally advanced levels, said Sun Zhen, a researcher at the Guangzhou Marine Geological Survey (GMGS) in south China. Following the standards of the International Ocean Discovery Program for the first time, researchers also completed on-site multi-parameter processing and analysis of the samples, including cataloging, cutting, scanning, testing and storage, thereby mastering full-process operational capabilities for ultra-deep water ocean scientific drilling. The samples and data obtained during the voyage provide crucial empirical evidence for addressing core scientific issues such as the expansion of the South China Sea. They are also of great significance for studying the evolution of the ancient marine environment in the sea and for the exploration and development of ultra-deep water energy resources, researchers noted. A total of 170 researchers from nine institutions participated in the voyage, which was organized by the China Geological Survey and implemented by the GMGS. China's first domestically-built ocean drilling vessel, Mengxiang, was officially commissioned in 2024. ■ China's ocean drilling vessel Mengxiang conducts a deep-sea sample drilling operation on July 29, 2026. item.title: China's industrial profits retain double-digit growth via high-tech, new growth drivers
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China's industrial profits maintained double-digit growth in the first eight months of 2026, driven by rapid expansion of high-tech manufacturing and new growth drivers, official figures showed on Monday. Profits of industrial firms above designated size increased 15.7 percent year on year during the first eight months of 2026, according to National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data. These industrial firms with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.97 million U.S. dollars) saw their combined profits reach 5.27 trillion yuan in the January-August period. In August alone, profits of major industrial firms grew 4.2 percent year on year, the NBS noted. Yu Weining, an NBS statistician, attributed this relatively fast profit growth to the steady advance of industrial production and a widened increase in industrial product prices. Earlier data revealed that the country's industrial output rose 5.3 percent in the first eight months of the year, while the producer price index, which measures costs of goods at the factory gate, climbed 3.8 percent year on year in August. Yu highlighted the electronic sector as the main pillar supporting industrial growth, with profits surging 110 percent year on year, contributing 62 percent to the overall profit growth of industrial firms. "The accelerated expansion of new technology applications, represented by artificial intelligence, has driven the expansion of demand in related fields, propelling swift profit growth in the electronics industry," Yu said. Yu noted that rising chip demand driven by emerging scenarios such as new energy vehicles, the Internet of Things and computing power centers had boosted profits in the optoelectronic device manufacturing and semiconductor discrete device manufacturing industries by 72 percent and 51.8 percent, respectively. High-tech manufacturing played a prominent role in driving growth. During the January-August period, profits of high-tech manufacturing firms above designated size soared 54.7 percent year on year, 39 percentage points higher than the overall growth rate. Profits of raw material manufacturing jumped 47.3 percent year on year in the January-August period, contributing 6.2 percentage points to the overall profit growth. Higher international crude oil and non-ferrous metals prices, meanwhile, helped lift chemical and non-ferrous metals profits in this period, while petroleum processing recovered from making losses to generating profits. Industrial firms' unit costs continued to decline in the January-August period, with cost per 100 yuan of operating revenue down 0.41 yuan year on year, while the profit margin on operating revenue rose 0.44 percentage points to 5.66 percent, reflecting improved cost control and profitability. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) highlights the development of a modern industrial system anchored by advanced manufacturing. The country will move to upgrade traditional sectors to the mid-to-high end of the value chain, nurture emerging industries, and make forward-looking plans for industries of the future, according to this development blueprint. Looking ahead, Yu said efforts should be made to expand domestic demand, optimize supply, accelerate the shift from old growth drivers to new ones, and promote the sustained development of the industrial economy with new and improved quality. ■

item.title: China opens four high-speed rail lines, expanding national network
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Singers from Ankang City perform on G9997, the first train of the Xi'an-Ankang high-speed railway, in northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Sept. 28, 2026. The Xi'an-Ankang high-speed railway was officially put into operation on Monday, cutting the railway travel time between Xi'an and Ankang to less than one hour. Spanning about 171 kilometers and with a design speed of 350 kilometers per hour, the railway runs through the cities of Xi'an, Shangluo and Ankang in Shaanxi Province and has five stations along the line. (Xinhua/Shao Rui) BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China, home to the world's largest high-speed rail network, opened four major high-speed railway sections to traffic on Monday, improving transport links across several regions. The new sections connect Xiong'an in Hebei Province with Shangqiu in Henan Province, Xi'an with Ankang in Shaanxi Province, Yichang with Xingshan in Hubei Province, and Harbin with Yichun in Heilongjiang Province. Spanning northern, northwestern, central and northeastern China, the new lines will facilitate travel for residents, improve regional connectivity and support economic development. ■ Constructors, railway staff and passengers pose for a photo on a train running along the Xiong'an-Shangqiu high-speed railway on Sept. 28, 2026. A new railway connecting Xiong'an New Area in north China's Hebei Province with Shangqiu in central China's Henan Province started operation on Monday. The railway travel time between Xiong'an and Shangqiu was shortened to 2 hours and 27 minutes. The 552-kilometer new line is a part of China's artery of the Beijing-Hong Kong Railway. item.title: Eighth round of China-U.S. economic and trade consultations yields positive consensus: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China and the United States held the eighth round of their economic and trade consultations in New York and Washington, D.C., the United States, from Sept. 20 to 23, reaching positive consensus that contributes to the economic and trade outcomes of the meeting of the two heads of state, China's Ministry of Commerce said on Monday. The two sides agreed to establish the Board of Trade under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism, with the primary target of optimizing bilateral trade, the ministry noted in a statement. The ministry said the Board of Trade will provide an important platform and institutional guarantee for the two countries to continuously expand the list of cooperation and shorten the list of problems in economic and trade affairs. To implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, China and the United States have held multiple rounds of consultations under the Board of Trade framework on an arrangement for a 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reduction, and have reached consensus, the ministry said. The two sides agreed to reduce tariffs on about 30 billion U.S. dollars' worth of goods imported from each other on a reciprocal basis, with tariffs on around 90 percent of the covered products to be lowered to most-favored-nation rates. These reductions will be implemented simultaneously after each side completes domestic legal procedures, according to the ministry. The economic and trade teams of the two sides agreed to include Chinese coal imports from the United States in the reciprocal tariff reduction framework, which is expected to facilitate Chinese coal imports from the United States in 2027 and 2028, the ministry revealed. Importing U.S. coal will complement China's domestic coal market while providing stable revenue and employment for the U.S. coal industry, helping to stabilize and expand bilateral trade, the ministry explained. The two sides also agreed on lists of products subject to the 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reductions, based on their respective market needs and industrial interests. The United States will reduce tariffs on Chinese imports including toys, home appliances, baby products, kitchen and bathroom goods, and holiday gifts, while China will lower tariffs on U.S. imports including agricultural products, personal care products, medical devices and coal, according to the ministry. The two sides will jointly release their respective lists of products covered by the tariff reductions, the ministry added. This arrangement is expected to help stabilize bilateral trade and create more favorable conditions for Chinese exports to the U.S. market, while meeting domestic market demand and strengthening trade cooperation in agricultural products, energy, manufactured goods and consumer goods, the ministry noted. In the consultations, China and the United States also agreed to establish the Board of Investment under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism. It will provide an institutionalized communication platform for both sides, with the two countries' economic and trade teams conducting regular dialogue on potential investment opportunities and barriers, the ministry said. The two sides further agreed to establish an agricultural working group under the Board of Trade, to be co-chaired by China's Ministry of Commerce and the Office of the United States Trade Representative, with participation from relevant regulatory agencies of both countries, said the ministry. The working group will discuss issues including two-way market access and regulatory matters for agricultural products. Both sides agreed to hold the working group's first meeting before the end of 2026, the ministry said. The two sides reached a consensus in principle on financial services. China will examine and approve applications from financial service institutions of all countries, including those with U.S. capital, to conduct business and establish branches in China. China hopes the United States will also provide a fair, transparent and stable policy environment for Chinese financial institutions, said the ministry. As the two sides' lead negotiators under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent established a dialogue on artificial intelligence (AI) and held their first discussion on AI-related risks and benefits. The two sides agreed to hold the next dialogue before the end of November this year and to set up a communication channel for AI incidents. On the basis of extending the joint arrangements of economic and trade consultations in Kuala Lumpur through Jan. 10, 2027, China and the United States agreed to continue actively discussing the issue, with a view to reaching a mutually agreed solution. Such an arrangement, on the one hand, gives both sides room to take stock of and assess the implementation of the joint arrangements and consider how to move China-U.S. economic and trade relations forward. On the other hand, by combining a time-bound extension with continued active discussions, it provides a relatively stable and predictable policy environment for cooperation between businesses of the two countries, according to the ministry. It is believed that the two sides will continue their efforts and seek a positive solution on a further extension through high-level economic and trade interactions before the end of the year, the ministry noted. The two sides also exchanged views on increasing direct passenger flights between the two countries, agreeing to maintain communication on increasing China-U.S. flights and related matters. Since last year, China and the United States have held eight rounds of economic and trade consultations. During the latest consultations, the two sides reaffirmed and renewed their commitment to fully implementing the consensus reached in previous rounds of economic and trade talks, which will help create favorable conditions and a stable environment for bilateral economic and trade cooperation, while also contributing to global economic growth, said the ministry. ■

item.title: Skills on display, employment changes in motion at WorldSkills Shanghai
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
* The seven new skills making their debut at the WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai offer clues to where economic demand is heading, reflecting growth in areas ranging from the digital economy and smart manufacturing to service consumption. * Artificial intelligence is reshaping what happens inside jobs, expanding what workers are expected to do and changing the division of labor between humans and technology. * China is updating vocational programs, expanding skills training and strengthening links between schools and industry to keep talent supply in step with rapidly evolving industry demand. by Xinhua writers Ding Yinghua and Zhou Rui SHANGHAI, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- A drone assembled from scores of parts navigated its way around obstacles. A mobile robot, after programming and fine-tuning by a competitor, identified and grasped objects. In a mock store, meanwhile, another competitor arranged merchandise, served customers, and switched between in-store sales and livestreaming. Over four days at the 48th WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai, scenes involving 64 skills told a broader story of economic transformation: new technologies and shifting market needs are creating fresh demand, job roles are being reshaped, and the skills economies need are evolving with them. With all competition events completed, the global skills gathering is set to conclude with a closing ceremony on Sunday. This year's edition brought together 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions, while seven skills made their debuts, including unmanned aerial systems, software testing and retail. Francis Hourant, president of WorldSkills International, said trades today are not exactly the same as they were in the 1960s, adding that the competition adjusts its portfolio to stay connected with "the reality of the industry." NEW DEMAND TAKING SHAPE The seven newcomers in Shanghai offer some of the clearest clues to where economic demand is moving. In the unmanned aerial systems arena, competitors began with around 200 separate components. They had to assemble and calibrate a drone, write the code and prepare it for autonomous flight. Once airborne, this drone was expected to scan an unfamiliar environment, map obstacles and plan its own route -- with no human intervention during the flight. Beyond the competition, similar technologies are already finding their way into everyday life. In Shenzhen in south China, drones deliver takeout to smart pickup lockers, while in southwest China's Chengdu, urban logistics drones carry goods along regular low-altitude routes, and over rice fields in northeast China, agricultural drones have become part of routine farm work. Retail presented a different scene at the Shanghai event, but still reflected the same trend. Across different modules, competitors had to take on multiple roles: arranging merchandise, pitching products to customers, hosting livestreams and handling unexpected complaints. "We are not training simply a top salesperson, but an all-round retail expert," said Chen Ying, head of the expert group at the Shanghai training base for this skill. Such a combination of skills reflects a consumer market increasingly extending beyond goods toward services and experiences. In the first eight months of 2026, China's service retail sales rose 4.9 percent year on year, outpacing the 1-percent growth in goods retail sales, as demand expanded in areas including tourism, culture, sports and leisure. "Where industries develop, new occupations emerge, and WorldSkills sets up skills accordingly," said Zhang Rui, deputy director of the WorldSkills Competition China (Tianjin) Research Center. Among the seven new skills, software testing and digital interactive media design reflect the rise of the digital economy, while unmanned aerial systems and rail vehicle technology are among the skills tied to smart manufacturing and advanced equipment, Zhang explained. AI REWRITING THE JOB If changing demand helps explain why new occupations are emerging, artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping what happens inside a job. In the web technologies competition, contestants are no longer assessed simply on their ability to write code. They must analyze user needs, decide what functions a business scenario requires, complete front- and back-end development, and deliver a finished product. Wu Yingxiang, a technical expert and coach for the Chinese team in WorldSkills web technologies, said AI is making code generation much faster, thus expanding what programmers are expected to do. "Every programmer may now become a project manager and a product manager," he said. At another hall, contestants in the digital interactive media design competition moved from product planning to image processing, video production and interaction design during more than 20 hours of competition across four days. Notably, even as AI begins to take over some basic work in the industry, the training remains highly demanding. Zhou Jiaxiang, a member of China's national training squad for this skill, described a six-hour video-production module in which contestants may have to adjust dozens or even hundreds of parameters and fine-tune transition effects frame by frame. Data show that demand for AI-related skills has risen rapidly in China. Newly posted campus-recruitment positions in AI surged 47.3 percent year on year in the first five months of 2026, according to data from the talent research arm of Maimai, a Chinese networking and recruitment platform. For Hourant, this shift points to a changing division of labor rather than an either/or choice between humans and AI. "It is not AI in the end," he said, adding that the future lies in combining human skills with AI. BUILDING SKILLS FOR TOMORROW The skills on display in Shanghai point to a challenge, namely whether the supply of skilled workers can keep pace with industries that are evolving faster than before. Official data reveal that China has more than 220 million skilled workers, including over 72 million highly skilled workers. Yet gaps remain in fast-growing sectors. According to the Ministry of Education, China faced a shortage of more than 10 million highly skilled workers in areas related to the digital economy and intelligent manufacturing in 2025, making the expansion of skilled talent a top priority. The country has been stepping up efforts to reduce this shortfall. The ministry added 27 programs to the country's vocational education catalog in July, covering fields like the digital economy, AI, the low-altitude economy and advanced equipment, with new offerings related to humanoid robots, to better match talent supply with emerging and future industries. Over 5.5 million instances of subsidized vocational skills training were provided in the first half of 2026, with programs focusing on areas such as AI, advanced manufacturing, new-energy vehicles and the low-altitude economy, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security noted. Shanghai Information Technology College, for example, has added four programs tailored to the city's AI industry and brought real production scenarios, technical standards and company projects into the teaching environment. Elsewhere, schools are strengthening links with industry to keep training in step with swiftly changing industry needs. At Jiangxi Software Vocational and Technical University in east China, the campus is integrated with an industrial park, with nearly 100 companies involved in tailored training. Enterprise engineers teach classes, while real commercial projects are brought onto campus. "Vocational education cannot be run behind closed doors," said Vice Principal of Shanghai Information Technology College Sun Pengtao. "Programs have to be updated along with industry." (Video reporters: Ding Ting and Zhou Rui; Video editors: Hong Liang and Zhu Cong) ■
